review_notes: Reviewed all 242 lines, including the definitions and proofs, and inspected the related axis-height definitions and uses in HittingWords.lean and ExperimentContact.lean. The proposed simp attributes follow the existing rewrite direction; I did not run Lean or claim that any change was tested.

findings.excerpt:
lemma axisHeight_opposite {d : ℕ} (e : Step d) (x : Site d) :
    axisHeight (oppositeStep e) x = -axisHeight e x := by
  rcases e with ⟨i,b⟩
  cases b <;> simp [axisHeight,oppositeStep]

lemma axisHeight_neg {d : ℕ} (e : Step d) (x : Site d) :
    axisHeight e (-x) = -axisHeight e x := by
  rcases e with ⟨i,b⟩
  cases b <;> simp [axisHeight]
findings.problem: These linearity identities are not in the simp set, so expressions involving an opposite step or a negated site do not simplify to the signed height form automatically. This file already has to name the lemmas explicitly in proofs (including the anchor-height and forced-contact proofs), and related proofs also use explicit rewrites for opposite-step heights.
findings.proposed_change: Add `[simp]` to both lemma declarations, preserving their current left-to-right orientation. The desired normal forms are `-axisHeight e x` for both `axisHeight (oppositeStep e) x` and `axisHeight e (-x)`. These rules reduce the structural form on the left and do not introduce a reverse height expression, so they have no apparent rewrite cycle.
findings.benefit: Simplification can normalize these common height expressions without repeatedly listing the lemmas, making the existing proofs and downstream goals involving signed paths easier to simplify.
